quest.title: The Truth of What Was
quest.description: The many-layered mysterious case caused by cosmetics has now been fully solved, and after Sigewinne finishes helping the Marechaussee Phantom wind up the case, she prepares to tell you a story about the past...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x325, Primogem x60, Mora x22000, Guide to Equity x5, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x5

talks.objective: Take a look around the Court of Fontaine

dialogues.speaker: Calcagni
dialogues.text: The wait is over, everyone! The sale of our new skincare product, Romaritime Essence, will now begin!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Another skincare promotion? And it's selling as fast as last time! Wonder what people would think if they knew what was in that last batch...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Sigewinne's here too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Sigewinne!

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: #Oh, {NICKNAME}, Paimon, hello! I hope you two got a good rest yesterday after all your hard work?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course! Nurse's orders, right? ...Anyway, are you here to take notes for your next article?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Actually, I'm mostly here to help Officer Morgane wrap up yesterday's case.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, that reminds Paimon... That stuff sold like crazy, didn't it! Is it gonna cause huge problems?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Nope, there's nothing to worry about. Unless modified, Butterfly Dew is an excellent skincare product that's completely safe to use.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Besides, officers have already retrieved all Butterfly Dew purchased on the market. Now, it's just a matter of disposal.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: After consulting Monsieur Neuvillette, I came up with a way to neutralize any harmful effects, so it'll evaporate naturally without polluting the water or soil.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! It's Sigewinne to the rescue again!

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Thank you for serving as our consultant, Head Nurse. All the Butterfly Dew we recovered has been disposed of according to your instructions.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Great. Good job, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Also, you mentioned you wanted a copy of Rawat's interrogation records... Well, technically Potton's records... Anyway, I have them with me. Here.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: After he saw his mother for the last time, it was like all his mental defenses came crashing down. He put up no resistance during the interrogation, and answered all our questions. We learned a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Apparently, the formula was something he discovered by chance while helping the criminal gang produce Sinthe. Later, he came up with the idea to dilute it and use the resulting substance as a skincare product.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Their supplier was Vacher — but you could also argue that they were the ones doing him a favor. His operation helped Vacher's gang dispose of an enormous amount of evidence.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: It made for a seamless collaboration. One man's trash was another man's treasure, and there were no loose ends. It's no wonder we never noticed what Potton's gang was up to.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Vacher again, huh... Is there still no end to the harm he caused?

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Make no mistake, the crimes of Vacher and his accomplices will come to an end. It's only a matter of time.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Since the flood cut off their supply of Primordial Seawater, they've been forced to resort to riskier methods — like using their private reserve to attack people on the street. Naturally, those attempts all ended in failure.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: After receiving numerous reports, we were able to zero in on the gang and eventually round them up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That sounds more like it!

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Based on what he told us in his confession, we pretty much had him backed into a corner, even though he made a point of distancing himself from the gang while disguised as Rawat.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: He tried to throw us off his tail by reporting his accomplices, giving him enough time to transform back into Potton and see his mother one last time.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: But, there was one thing he hadn't anticipated... Even though "Potton" had been missing for a long time, we were very much still on the lookout for him. So the moment he appeared in public after changing back to his original appearance, we caught him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So he tried this once before, huh? Guess he really did want his mother to see him again. But in the end...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: ...Looking at the interrogation records, it seems like he spent the first sum of money he earned as Rawat on his mother's treatment.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Yes, which is why I suspect that his initial motive for using the potion was not personal greed, but a desire to become somebody who had the power to save her.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Even so, he went too far. In the end, he got what he deserved.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I understand. Thank you for bringing me these records.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why did you want them, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Potton was one of my patients, so I need to put together a medical file for him. My teacher always stressed that a person's life experiences are just as important to their file as their medical history.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why are you still treating him like your patient? Isn't he kinda beyond redemption now?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: That may be true, but a patient is a patient, regardless of the choices that bring them to my care.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Ah, one last thing, Head Nurse. Please keep everything you know about this potion a secret.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: It would be for the best if most of Fontaine knows nothing of its existence. I know my fellow officers and I will be able to sleep easier if that's the case.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Of course. Not to worry.

dialogues.speaker: Morgane
dialogues.text: Thank you for understanding. I'll take my leave, then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So Sigewinne, did you really use that potion yourself?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Why do you sound so surprised, Paimon? I told you all about it. It was quite a while ago now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... You mean that story about the witch and the potion? So it was really, actually, genuinely a true story?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Yes. It really, actually, genuinely was.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The process of making that potion...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I know. There are some secrets I can't tell anyone about. But considering everything we've been through together, I know I can trust you with them.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Before I tell you, though, could you follow me somewhere? I want to pay my respects to an old friend.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course!

talks.objective: Go to the place you agreed upon with Sigewinne

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... Neuvillette and Wriothesley! They're here too!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: #Good to see you, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. I trust all has been going well for you.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Big news, everyone: The Iudex is out of his office on important business.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Hmm? Is that genuinely something people would consider "big news"?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Why wouldn't they? Important business is a big deal.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Ah... Yes, you're quite right. When someone you care about requires emotional support, being there for them at the right time and place is of the utmost importance.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: After reading the Marechaussee Phantom's reports, I had a feeling a trip here might be in order.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Take note — that, my friends, is how Monsieur Neuvillette shows that he cares. We're both here for the same purpose, actually — to accompany Sigewinne as she pays her respects to her late teacher.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So the old friend she mentioned was her teacher then? The "witch"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, sorry, sorry, Paimon didn't mean to be rude! It's only 'cause Sigewinne calls her that all the time, so...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I doubt she considers that title to be offensive, Paimon. Don't worry.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Indeed. In fact, I believe Sigewinne would take it as a sign of affection. She has spoken of this doctor on many occasions, and it sounds like she was a truly generous individual.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: In those days, many people harbored prejudices against Melusines. She was the only teacher willing to take Sigewinne on as a student.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, it's really nice of you two to be here for Sigewinne! Guess you guys really look out for your younger colleagues, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Younger colleague? That might be true for the Iudex, but I'm not sure I can say the same.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Sigewinne served a sentence in the Fortress of Meropide hundreds of years ago, and after she did her time, she decided to stick around. She's been an integral part of our administration ever since.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Strictly speaking, the head nurse has been around longer than most people in the Fortress, myself included. Pretty sure that makes me the younger colleague.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She served a sentence?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She committed a crime?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Yes. Long before I became Iudex, there was an ancient law in Fontaine that prohibited any attempt to transform another species into a human.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Initially, I and most researchers believed this law to have been imposed due to ethical concerns.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: But now, it seems more likely that the law was nothing more than an insurance policy — a way for Egeria to ensure that her people would remain insulated from the truth, thus enabling them to lead more straightforward, happier lives.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Ignorance is bliss, as they say.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Sigewinne had her reasons for choosing to obtain a human form, but the act was nonetheless in clear violation of the law.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Could you tell us a bit more about what happened back then?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Certainly. Sigewinne does not object to her close friends learning about her history. In fact, I first learned of it myself because she confessed the truth to me of her own volition...

dialogues.speaker: "The Witch"
dialogues.text: Even with their daughter so ill, they kicked you out? Stubborn as always... and prejudice isn't a disease I can cure, either.

dialogues.speaker: "The Witch"
dialogues.text: *sigh* Shame that I don't have the energy to get over there. You're laughable, you old witch. You want to save everyone in Fontaine, but you can't even save the patient before you.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Master, what are you...

dialogues.speaker: "The Witch"
dialogues.text: I discovered a strange disease, one I suspect that every Fontainian suffers from. But without witnesses or proof, no one will believe me.

dialogues.speaker: "The Witch"
dialogues.text: I had no choice but to experiment on myself to find a cure, but I hit a wall — and as you can see, it took a wretched toll on me.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Then... I'll find a cure for you, and then you can go cure her!

dialogues.speaker: "The Witch"
dialogues.text: There's no need... I'm beyond saving now. There's nothing you can do.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: But Master...

dialogues.speaker: "The Witch"
dialogues.text: As I said before, a doctor's duty is to treat whatever ailments they can.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I know... But, they don't trust me at all.

dialogues.speaker: "The Witch"
dialogues.text: *cough* That girl... She's your first ever patient, isn't she? ...Tell me, what cost are you willing to bear to see her cured?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I'll do whatever it takes.

dialogues.speaker: "The Witch"
dialogues.text: Even if it means breaking the law and being punished for it?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: ...As long as I don't hurt anyone, yes.

dialogues.speaker: "The Witch"
dialogues.text: Haha. Spoken like a true student of mine.

dialogues.speaker: "The Witch"
dialogues.text: Then I shall make one more final gamble... and see my experiment through to its end. Leave me for now, and come back in two hours.

dialogues.speaker: "The Witch"
dialogues.text: If I am able to work this miracle, then I will have found a way to save all Fontainians, and I shall be able to help you treat that girl.

dialogues.speaker: "The Witch"
dialogues.text: If not... Then it means there is one more disease in this world that I cannot treat. In that case, do not come looking for me.

dialogues.speaker: "The Witch"
dialogues.text: I will leave you a parting gift — an accidental discovery, happened upon through my study of this strange disease. It has little use, but it will at least help you cure this one patient you can reach.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: When Sigewinne returned, the miracle had not occurred.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: She found a potion bottle and a note on the table. After using the potion as instructed, she gained her current form, breaking Fontaine's law in the process.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: And after I had confirmed the veracity of the events, I gave my verdict.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's what happened...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: You're here.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: The old friend I mentioned was my teacher. When she passed, her body was nowhere to be found. All that's left of her is an empty tomb, and even that's deep underwater now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sigewinne... The witch who gave you the magic potion, she was your teacher, wasn't she?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Ah, sounds like Monsieur Neuvillette filled you in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: After learning the truth... it must've been hard to process, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Well... To be honest, after I realized what really happened that night, my first thought was that it kind of made sense. It seemed exactly like the sort of thing she would do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, she was planning to sacrifice herself, and never told you!

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: That's just who she was. If lying is what it took to get a kid to take their medicine, then that's what she'd do.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright... But, why did you turn yourself in?

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: I broke the law, simple as that. My teacher made her choice, and I made mine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: True, it's just... The way Potton framed it when he was asking you all those questions, it made Paimon really mad!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're not like him at all, and everything Neuvillette said confirms that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And yet you were still convicted and thrown in prison... It just feels so unfair.

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Unfair? I happen to think just the opposite. If I hadn't served that time, I'm not sure I would've been able to stay strong when he was questioning me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What makes you say that?

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: I knew you'd be curious. Let me tell you a story...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now that's an ending Paimon can get behind!

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: After hearing everything Potton said, I wanted to tell him that it didn't matter who he looked like on the outside... But it was too late — the warmth in his palm had already disappeared.

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: I tried to treat him, but... The roots of his problem had nothing to do with his face.

choices.text: No need to feel too bad for him.

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: I understand... Thanks, you two. I appreciate you being here for me while I talk this through.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, it's nothing! Our pleasure.

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Oh, there's one more reason I invited you here. It's about time I finally give you what I promised.

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: In order to restore the appearances of the face-swapping victims, the Marechaussee Phantom gave me special permission to make a few bottles of that potion. And... I made one extra, just for you two.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? We don't need it, though... Shouldn't we destroy it?

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Well, even if you chose to destroy it, I still thought I should give it to you first. You two did so much for me — how could I break my promise?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, fair enough. But anyway, Paimon's definitely not interested in this stuff anymore.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, if this is the very last bottle in all of Teyvat, getting rid of it would feel like kind of a waste... Maybe we can give it a special meaning somehow... Ooh, Paimon's got it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Melusine physiology wasn't affected by the great flood, right? So that means the potion should have a permanent effect on you. In that case... Whaddaya say, Sigewinne? Ever thought about transforming back to the way you used to look?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: After all, from a Melusine point of view, Paimon bets Melusines look the cutest of all!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon...

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Paimon, after everything, do you really think it matters whether I'm a Melusine or a human?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, well...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Heh, what was Paimon thinking? You made up your mind a long time ago. Yeah, let's just destroy this thing.

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Leave it to me.

choices.text: It does feel like wasted potential.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: On behalf of the Marechaussee Phantom, I would like to once again thank the Fortress of Meropide for your assistance in the response to yesterday's prisonbreak.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: #Our Head Nurse and {NICKNAME} and Paimon did most of the heavy lifting, I would say.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Sigewinne seems to be in good spirits. I trust work hasn't been too hard on her lately?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Well, she might be the only permanent medical staff in the Fortress, but there's plenty of people with medical knowledge willing to help her out.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I am most relieved to hear it.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Haha, the way you're asking after her wellbeing makes you sound like a concerned parent.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Ah, well, I won't lie... I've always seen myself that way.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Showing your age a bit there, don't you think...

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Indeed. Actually, I often forget just how much older I am than you...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Well, while we're on the topic... What did you do before getting this job, anyway? Spend all day swimming in the sea, from east to west, then north to south?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Yes, and uh... from the surface to the ocean floor, on occasion.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Wow. Impressive.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: ...Apologies, that was merely an attempt at humor. You can disregard what I said.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Hah, that's impossible, I'm afraid. My imagination's already running wild.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I'd like to stay here with my teacher for a little longer.

dialogues.speaker: Calcagni
dialogues.text: Stocks are running low, so purchase soon to avoid disappointment!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Potton is eventually taken away by members of the Marechaussee Phantom. A day passes in a flash.
